Thanks Jaspreet — looping in Dev (security/infra) and Ben (enterprise sales lead) so we can propose an ops-safe design. High level notes below; Dev, please expand with operational details and call out TODOs for the pilot.

High-level proposal (summary):
- Customer owns root keys (BYOK) in their KMS/HSM. Redwood will never persist unwrapped root key material.
- For hosted Private control plane scenarios we use envelope encryption: customer's root key (KMS/HSM) is used to wrap per-cluster Data Encryption Keys (DEKs). Redwood stores only the wrapped DEKs.
- For on-prem HSMs the Redwood on-prem agent performs local key wrapping and a stored token reference is sent to the control plane; the unwrapped DEK never leaves the customer boundary.
- Rotation: schedule rotates DEKs per-cluster and re-wraps existing encrypted artifacts; for live inference we support dual-key period allowing new traffic to use new DEK while old in-flight requests complete under the previous DEK.

Dev — can you add details on: agent authentication, wrapping/unwrapping latency profile, how we handle KV cache re-keying, and any fallback if the KMS endpoint is unavailable?

Mina — adding the technical playbook notes below for Jaspreet and ACME security. I kept it concise for the thread; I can follow up with a Confluence deep-dive.

1) Key hierarchy and envelope encryption:
   - Root Key (Customer KMS/HSM) => wraps Cluster DEK(s). Cluster DEKs encrypt storage volumes, KV cache keys, model artifacts at rest.
   - We use AES-GCM-256 for DEKs; wrapping uses RSA-OAEP / KMS-native wrapping.

2) On-Prem HSM workflow:
   - Redwood on-prem agent (running in ACME network) authenticates to local HSM via PKCS#11. Agent provisions a locally generated DEK and calls local HSM to wrap it with the customer root key.
   - Wrapped DEK blob and a short-lived agent certificate are recorded in the control plane registry. The unwrapped DEK stays in agent memory only.

3) Rotation strategy:
   - Planned rotation window: configurable (default quarterly).
   - Dual-DEK grace period: new DEK introduced; agent serves both new and old keys for N hours (configurable) to drain in-flight sessions.
   - Re-wrapping: for artifacts at rest we perform a background re-wrap job using staged workers; for large persisted model caches we re-wrap pointers rather than rewrite full object if using envelope-of-envelope approach.

4) Availability & fallback:
   - If KMS unreachable, agent uses cached wrapped-DEK and operates until cache TTL expires (configurable, default 6 hours).
   - If HSM operation fails for new key wrap, roll back and keep serving on previous key; alerting to SRE + ACME security.

5) KV/cache re-keying:
   - KV entries are stored encrypted under a per-node ephemeral key derived from cluster DEK; upon DEK rotation we re-encrypt metadata pointers and rotate ephemeral keys lazily on access (amortizes cost).

6) Attestations & audit:
   - We emit only wrap/unwarp audit events to the control plane (no plaintext). For Private with isolated control plane, audit logs can be pushed to customer S3/Log system via signed endpoint.

Latency notes:
   - Local wrap/unwarp: sub-50ms when HSM local to agent (depends on HSM model). KMS-managed wrap via cloud KMS typically 30-150ms depending on region. Envelope use keeps per-token inference latency impact minimal.

Jaspreet — quick answers inline and next steps below.

1) Audit event schema: we will emit the following fields in each wrap/unwarp event pushed to your S3 or to our control plane export:
   - timestamp (ISO 8601)
   - agent_id
   - cluster_id
   - operation_type (wrap | unwrap | rewrap)
   - key_id (customer key alias)
   - key_origin (KMS | HSM-local)
   - request_id (UUID)
   - status (success | failure)
   - latency_ms
   - initiating_principal (service-account or agent cert fingerprint)

2) KV-cache migration for large caches:
   - We'll run a staged re-wrap job that performs pointer-level re-wrapping for objects stored in object-store (cheap). For in-memory/node-local caches we do lazy re-key-on-access to avoid full copy. For the 2TB active model cache we'll provision parallel workers and estimate ~36-48 hours for a full re-wrap under the pilot config (we'll finalize runbook after a quick perf test).

- We'll update the SOW with monthly rotation addendum and estimated eng hours.

If that works, I'll mark this ready for SOW finalization.
